name: Tie formal necktie knots
blurb: Four knots — four-in-hand, half Windsor, full Windsor and a bow tie — cover every occasion, and each takes an evening to learn properly.
steps: Learn the four-in-hand: small, slightly asymmetric, and the right choice for most shirts and casual wear.
Learn the half Windsor: symmetrical and medium-sized, the safe default for business and interviews.
Learn the full Windsor: large and triangular, for spread collars and formal occasions.
Learn to get the length right — the tip should reach the middle of your belt buckle — by adjusting the starting position, which takes a few attempts each time.
Learn the dimple: pinch the fabric just below the knot as you tighten it, which is the detail that separates a good knot from a flat one.
Learn a real bow tie, which is just a shoelace bow done vertically and takes about twenty attempts before it clicks.
tips: Match knot size to collar spread: a narrow collar with a full Windsor looks wrong.
Never yank a tie undone by pulling the narrow end. Reverse the knot properly or it will crease permanently.
proof: You tie all four correctly, at the right length, with a dimple, without a mirror.
